chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When the believer is placed in his grave, it is called out: 'Indeed, the first of your gifts is Paradise, and the gift of the one who followed you (your coffin) is Forgiveness.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for a believer entering the grave and for those who follow the coffin?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) reveals the immediate spiritual rewards awaiting the deceased, framing the grave as a place of divine announcement rather than mere waiting. The 'first cloak' (hibaa) of Paradise signifies the honor bestowed upon the believer, while the forgiveness granted to those who followed the coffin highlights the communal merit of funeral processions in Shia tradition, encouraging active participation in burial rites.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the Believer enters his grave it is called out: ‘Indeed! The first of your gifts is the Paradise, and a gift of the one who followed you (your coffin), is the Forgiveness (from sins)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Sayf ibn ‘Ami rah from Jabir who has said the following: “Abu la’ far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
When a believing person is placed in the grave, it is announced then: “Paradise is the first gift for you and forgiveness for those who have escorted you.’””
